statement: The Arabs identified people by lineage and preserved genealogies carefully.

The agreed lineage: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim ibn Abd Manaf ibn Qusayy ibn Kilab ibn Murrah ibn Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib ibn Fihr ibn Malik ibn an-Nadr ibn Kinanah ibn Khuzaymah ibn Mudrikah ibn Ilyas ibn Mudar ibn Nizar ibn Ma'add ibn Adnan (21 fathers).
notes: Agreed upon by the genealogists; al-Bukhari gives the same chain in a chapter heading. Narrated as preserved lineage. Reviewer to check every name and the count of 21.

statement: Adnan descends from Ismail son of Ibrahim by agreement; the names between Adnan and Ismail are disputed.

Ibrahim left Hajar and the infant Ismail at the site of the Ka'bah with dates and water; her question and answer; her running between Safa and Marwah seven times; the angel at Zamzam and the water; Jurhum settling with her permission after seeing a bird; Ismail learned Arabic from them and married among them.
notes: Machine-checked against the dataset text of Bukhari 3364 on 2026-10-03. Direct speech follows the narration. The narration calls her 'the mother of Ismail'; the name Hajar is supplied.

statement: Ibrahim and Ismail raised the foundations of the House.
The Prophet said to men practising archery: 'Shoot, children of Ismail, for your father was an archer.'
notes: Machine-checked. The men were of the tribe of Aslam.

statement: Kinanah is among the descendants of Adnan; Fihr descends from Kinanah; the descendants of Fihr are called Quraysh.
alternatives: Some genealogists attach the name Quraysh to an-Nadr ibn Kinanah.

statement: Allah chose Kinanah from the children of Ismail, Quraysh from Kinanah, Banu Hashim from Quraysh, and him from Banu Hashim.
notes: Content machine-checked in the Sahih Muslim dataset (narrated by Wathilah ibn al-Asqa'); the Abd al-Baqi number 2276 is from memory and not machine-checked.

statement: Qusayy, the fifth forefather, gathered Quraysh in Makkah and took custodianship of the Ka'bah, the keys, the watering and feeding of pilgrims and the council.
Hashim's name was Amr; he was called Hashim for breaking bread into broth for the people of Makkah in a year of hunger.
Hashim established the winter journey to Yemen and the summer journey to Syria.
The Qur'an mentions the winter and summer journeys of Quraysh and calls them to worship the Lord of this House who fed them and made them safe.
Hashim married Salma bint Amr of Banu Najjar in Yathrib, died in Gaza, and she bore his son Shaybah in Yathrib.
Shaybah grew up in Yathrib; his uncle al-Muttalib brought him to Makkah; people took him for al-Muttalib's servant, hence the name Abd al-Muttalib.
Abd al-Muttalib became the leader of Quraysh.
Zamzam had been buried and forgotten; Abd al-Muttalib rediscovered and re-dug it.
notes: The dream that guided him is left out.

statement: At Hunayn the Prophet said: 'I am the Prophet, it is no lie; I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib.'
Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan about his lineage; Abu Sufyan said he was of noble lineage; Heraclius said messengers come from the noble families of their peoples.
notes: Machine-checked. Abu Sufyan was not yet a Muslim at the time.

statement: Abdullah was a son of Abd al-Muttalib, who married him to Aminah bint Wahb of Banu Zuhrah; Abdullah died not long after.
Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah and the seal of the prophets.
